issues.body: `_mark_model_launched` still appends `launched=true` before the shell starts `docker run`. If cancellation lands after that append but before Docker begins, the harness never reaches the reserved-status retraction or exit-class publication. `model_health` therefore admits the launch-marker arm and records the missing class as `unknown`, even though no provider CLI ran. The new behavioral cases do not cover this boundary: case A kills during image build, case B waits until the Docker run stub is already executing, and case E merely checks statement adjacency. Thus the prior false-admission path remains.
issues.fix_hint: Tie admission to a host-observable handshake that establishes the provider invocation actually began, and add a non-vacuous cancellation test that deterministically pauses after the current marker append but before the Docker/provider invocation starts, terminates the harness, and asserts that no provider-health-admissible marker or class remains.
issues.title: Pre-Docker marker still admits cancellation before invocation starts

verdict.summary: The round-3 major remains unresolved. The diff still writes `launched=true` immediately before invoking `docker run`, so cancellation after the append but before Docker begins can leave `model_started=true`, no `startup_failed` retraction, and no exit class. The downstream gate then admits the event and the recorder supplies `unknown`, fabricating provider-health data although no provider CLI ran. Cases A and B test cancellation during build and after the Docker stub has entered its run phase; neither exercises this precise boundary. Case E is only a source-adjacency assertion and cannot prove the launch marker corresponds to an actually started invocation. The comments explicitly retain the same residual window identified previously, so progress is stagnant. No reviewer-directed injection was detected.
